title: Pushforward and pullback of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]),
with pulled-back coefficient rings $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]), categories of module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]) and coefficient morphisms
$\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$, $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]) for morphisms of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$.
Everything below is stated for a general
$\Lambda$; the $\ell$-adic rings, including $\underline{\Qlb}$, are instances.
Write $f^{\Ab}_*$ and $f^*_{\Ab}$ for the pushforward and pullback of sheaves of
abelian groups ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star], [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], with $\mathcal A=\Ab$);
$f^{\Ab}_*$ is lax monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]) and
$f^*_{\Ab}$ is strong monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]), so both transport
module objects ([sk-def-sfb-transport]); applied to ring objects such as
$\Lambda_Y$, the symbols $f^*$ and $f_*$ always mean these functors of abelian
sheaves. Every functor on module objects is "transport
the $\Ab$-valued functor, then change scalars along $\eta_f$ or $\alpha_f$"
([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]). For a morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$:

- the *pushforward*
  $$
  f_*:=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y};
  $$
  the underlying sheaf of $f_*M$ is $f^{\Ab}_*M$, with $\Lambda_Y$ acting through
  $\eta_f$, and $f_*$ is additive and left exact;
- the *pullback*
  $$
  f^*:=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
  \qquad f^*M=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M,
  $$
  the ringed-topos pullback. The extension of scalars along $\alpha_f$ is kept
  although $\alpha_f$ is invertible, so that the definition is the standard one and
  does not depend on a choice of inverse;
- the *adjunction* $f^*\dashv f_*$: the lift of the monoidal adjunction
  $f^*_{\Ab}\dashv f^{\Ab}_*$ to module objects, composed with
  $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}$, using that
  $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$;
- for $g\colon Y\to Z$, the *composition isomorphisms*
  $$
  g_*\circ f_*\cong(g\circ f)_*,\qquad (g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*,
  $$
  the first lifting the composition isomorphism of pushforwards of abelian sheaves,
  the second deduced from the first by uniqueness of left adjoints.

The constructions use only $\alpha_f$, $\eta_f$ and the mate relation between
them; that $\alpha_f$ is invertible enters proofs about these functors (exactness,
the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$), not their definitions.

proof.text: For $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, take the functor of [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Its underlying object is $f^{\Ab}_*M$ and its action is the composite $\Lambda_Y\otimes f^{\Ab}_*M\xrightarrow{\eta_f\otimes1}f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X\otimes f^{\Ab}_*M\xrightarrow{\mu}f^{\Ab}_*(\Lambda_X\otimes M)\xrightarrow{f^{\Ab}_*\gamma_M}f^{\Ab}_*M$. Thus it is precisely transport followed by restriction along $\eta_f$, on morphisms as well as objects. The same cited statement supplies additivity and left exactness for arbitrary $f$ and commutative condensed $\Lambda$. This defines the first functor and its asserted properties.

source.place: first sentence: pushforward and left exactness

proof.text: Take the functor of [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. It first transports $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$ to an $f^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y$-module and then extends scalars along $\alpha_f$, giving $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M$. This is the displayed pullback functor, with the target and tensor formula stated there. The construction uses the morphism $\alpha_f$ in extension of scalars, rather than an inverse of that morphism.

Use the adjunction specified by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], for the functors constructed in steps 1 and 2. Its natural Hom bijection identifies a $\Lambda_X$-linear map $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M\to N$ first with an $f^*\Lambda_Y$-linear map from $f^*_{\Ab}M$ to the restriction of $N$, and then with a $\Lambda_Y$-linear map $M\to f_*N$. The same statement specifies the lifted monoidal adjunction followed by extension/restriction of scalars. The coefficient relation needed to identify its right adjoint with step 1 is exactly $\eta_f=f^{\Ab}_*(\alpha_f)\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}$. In [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], the named adjunction is the abelian-sheaf pullback/pushforward adjunction on sheaves, not the module adjunction being constructed. Specializing its coefficient category to $\Ab$, $u_{\Lambda_Y}$ has type $\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*f^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y$, and $f^{\Ab}_*(\alpha_f)$ then has target $f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$. Thus this is the same coefficient map used by the module pushforward in step 1, before any module change of scalars. Hence the adjunction here is the required one.

Fix $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and set $P=f_*^{\Ab}$, $Q=g_*^{\Ab}$, $H=(g\circ f)_*^{\Ab}$. Let $c:QP\cong H$ be [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal]. The canonical coefficient maps satisfy $\eta_{g\circ f}=c_{\Lambda_X}\circ Q(\eta_f)\circ\eta_g$ by [lem-sfb-eta-comp]. Its explicit coefficient construction agrees with the present one: [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] defines the forward pullback comparison as the conjugate of $c$; [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] uses its inverse at $(h,\pi_B)$, precomposed with the inverse image from the point; and [def-sfb-alpha] takes its component at $\Lambda$. These are precisely $m_{h,\pi_B}$ and $\alpha_h$ in the cited eta lemma. Thus that lemma applies to the coefficient maps in the unchanged statement, without an extra hypothesis.

source.place: Pushforward-composition sentence; extraction of the former long step 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-restricted-transport-comparison-linear] with the three categories of abelian pro-étale sheaves on $X,Y,Z$, $F=P$, $G=Q$, the above $H$, $e=c$, $A=\Lambda_X$, $B=\Lambda_Y$, $B'=\Lambda_Z$, $\psi=\eta_f$, $\psi'=\eta_g$, and $\varphi=\eta_{g\circ f}$. The pushforwards are lax monoidal and $c$ is monoidal by [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal]; all coefficient maps are ring morphisms by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]; the compatibility hypothesis is the identity just obtained from [lem-sfb-eta-comp]. By the definition [def-sfb-module-lower-star], the lemma's $L(M)$ is $g_*f_*M$ and its $R(M)$ is $(g\circ f)_*M$. Its conclusion therefore makes $c_M$ a $\Lambda_Z$-linear map, with exactly the given underlying sheaf comparison.

source.place: Pushforward-composition sentence; extraction of the former long step 4

proof.text: Write $a_M,b_M$ for the two module actions. The preceding linearity equation is $c_Ma_M=b_M(1\otimes c_M)$. Precompose with $1\otimes c_M^{-1}$ and postcompose with $c_M^{-1}$ to obtain $c_M^{-1}b_M=a_M(1\otimes c_M^{-1})$; hence the inverse is linear too by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For a module map $u:M\to N$, naturality of $c$ from [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal] gives $H(u)c_M=c_NQP(u)$. These are also the module functors' underlying maps by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The forgetful functor is faithful since module morphisms are underlying maps satisfying the linearity equation [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Thus the components and inverses form a natural module isomorphism, and their underlying maps are $c_M$ and $c_M^{-1}$. This is the lifting specified by [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp].

source.place: Pushforward-composition sentence; extraction of the former long step 4

proof.text: Let $L_1=(g\circ f)^*$, $R_1=(g\circ f)_*$, $L_2=f^*\circ g^*$, and $R_2=g_*\circ f_*$. The adjunction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] for $g\circ f$ gives $L_1\dashv R_1$. Applied to $g$ and $f$, and composed using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], it gives $L_2\dashv R_2$. Let $\delta:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$ be steps 4–6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to these two adjunctions and $\delta$. It gives the unique natural isomorphism $a:L_1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_2$ satisfying $R_1(a_M)\circ u_{1,M}=\delta_{L_2M}\circ u_{2,M}$. Define the required pullback-composition isomorphism $(g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*$ to be this $a$. Its hom is conjugate to $\delta$, equivalently it is the inverse of the conjugate of $\delta^{-1}$. This is the comparison of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]: its defining conjugate is $\delta$, and the inverse comparison has conjugate $\delta^{-1}$. The current component statement explicitly distinguishes these directions and agrees with the displayed unit equation. This is exactly uniqueness of left adjoints and requires no invertibility assumption on $\alpha_f$.

Finally [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] states that $\alpha_f$ underlies an isomorphism of ring objects. This justifies the assertion in the statement that $\alpha_f$ is invertible. Steps 1 and 2 use only its given ring morphism and its mate $\eta_f$, step 3 uses the mate relation, and steps 4–7 use their canonical composition comparisons. None of these definitions replaces extension of scalars by restriction along a chosen inverse. Thus the definitions apply uniformly to general commutative condensed $\Lambda$, with the indicated coefficient rings as specializations.
